source.title: A Two-Scale Complexity Measure for Deep Learning Models
source.authors: Massimiliano Datres; G. P. Leonardi; Alessio Figalli; David Sutter

record.tranche_reason: The paper proposes and evaluates a Fisher-information-based complexity measure, but its experiments relate that measure to training loss, not to the training–test gap or any listed version’s outcome.
record.gate_note: The generalization bound is theoretical. The empirical results concern complexity estimates and training loss; no test error, generalization gap, random-label fit, or magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness is reported.
record.test_reason: The study proves a generalization bound for a new Fisher-information capacity measure and compares that measure with training loss. It reports no held-out performance or magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure, so its results do not test V1–V8. The batch-size experiments also report only training loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate about the empirical scope but omits the theoretical contribution: the authors prove a generalization bound involving 2sED, find lower 2sED closely approximates it in their simulations, and relate lower 2sED to training behavior as evidence for potential training-free model selection. They do not empirically demonstrate that it tracks training–test gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates Fisher-information-based effective dimension and relates it to training loss; it does not use the interventions or measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training-loss ranking changes with the number of training data: MLP 54-16-7 is lower at 10000 samples, while MLP 54-13-11-9-7 is consistently better at 100000.

fits_no_version.finding: Among the compared Covertype MLPs, MLP 54-16-7 achieves lower training loss with 10000 samples, whereas MLP 54-13-11-9-7 performs better with 100000 samples. The authors relate these rankings to scale-dependent lower 2sED.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower 2sED captures differences in training capabilities across architectures and training-set sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5.1 bounds the uniform population–empirical risk difference using 2sED under stated regularity assumptions. It does not establish the magnitude-aware sharpness ranking described in V7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-scale effective dimension provides a theoretical generalization bound under the theorem's assumptions.

record.problems: The reported training-loss curves are figures without extracted numerical values or stated uncertainty. The paper reports no held-out error or training–test gap for these experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Other plotted training-loss curves and effective-dimension comparisons are not extracted because the text does not describe their outcomes in enough detail to assign a result beyond the figures.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Held-out comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons on held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its correlation with training–test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies the paper as a preprint under review; it does not substantiate the record's peer-reviewed venue entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label test performance, and chance-level test accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and architectural bias.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons on held-out performance.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
